rationale: Mirtazapine (NaSSA: α2-antagonist, 5-HT2/3 antagonist, H1 blocker; t½ ~20–40h; sedating; significant weight gain) to agomelatine (MT1/MT2 agonist; t½ ~2h; weight neutral; much less sedating). Switch reasons: weight gain, excessive sedation, or metabolic concerns on mirtazapine. As mirtazapine is reduced, H1 blockade and noradrenergic effects reduce — insomnia may re-emerge (agomelatine helps sleep but less potently than mirtazapine's H1 blockade). No pharmacodynamic serotonin syndrome risk. Baseline LFTs before starting agomelatine. Taper mirtazapine to avoid sleep disruption during withdrawal. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start agomelatine 25 mg nocte (same time as mirtazapine). Continue mirtazapine 30 mg. CHECK BASELINE LFTs. Warn: sleep quality may temporarily worsen as mirtazapine is reduced (H1 blockade being withdrawn). Agomelatine will help sleep continuity but is less sedating.
Reduce mirtazapine to 15 mg. Continue agomelatine 25 mg. Monitor sleep and mood. Some rebound insomnia possible.

Stop mirtazapine. Continue agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Sleep may be lighter than on mirtazapine — set expectations. Titrate agomelatine to 50 mg at 2 weeks if response inadequate. Appetite and weight should begin to normalise over 4–8 weeks.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Mirtazapine 30 mg → agomelatine 25 mg (start dose). Not pharmacologically equivalent — different mechanisms. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

contraindications: ALT >3× ULN at baseline — do not start agomelatine.
